---
name: apple-hig
description: Use when designing, implementing, or reviewing interfaces for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, CarPlay, or other Apple system experiences using Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Routes to current platform, foundation, pattern, component, input, and technology guidance.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: AyushRajSinghParihar
  source: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support, product feasibility, or platform adaptation, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. Before finalizing the route, search the [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md)
   for the task's concepts as well as component or framework names. Its trigger
   descriptions connect everyday product requests to Apple's topic names; users
   need not name an Apple framework. Read the owning family and matching topic
   procedure before its supporting reference. Search relevant rows instead of
   loading the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

# Apple HIG: Commands, roles and discoverable surfaces

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Inventory each command’s outcome, scope, availability and reversibility. Distinguish immediate commands from persistent selection before entering Buttons, Toggles, or the appropriate menu procedure.
2. Choose a discoverable primary surface plus contextual shortcuts. On Mac, consider the menu bar’s command catalog and keyboard access even when a toolbar or context menu also exposes the action.
3. Use consequence and current task to decide role/default, confirmation and recovery. Consult Alerts and Undo and redo when that decision depends on destructive behavior; preserve documented exceptions.
4. Deliver an action contract naming labels, roles, surfaces, shortcuts, availability and relevant pending/resolved behavior. Verify the action and its recovery rather than color alone.

## Enter the topic procedure

Read the selected topic’s SKILL.md before its supporting guidance. For a review,
inspect actual evidence and return findings; for an implementation request, make
the authorized change; for design or adaptation, produce a usable specification
or patch. Load related topics only when the chosen procedure calls for them.

# Apple HIG: Map user actions to input and alternatives

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify the action and available hardware/input context, then enter the keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controller, Pencil, Crown or sensor procedure.
2. Preserve reserved system gestures and familiar input meanings. Separate targeting, focus, selection and activation; define feedback and reachable alternatives for the actions people must complete.
3. Account for comfort, precision, fatigue and switching between available inputs. Custom inputs should not remove an accessible route to an essential action.
4. Deliver an action-to-input mapping, focus/selection states and observable verification scenarios. Keep code/static observations separate from physical comfort, eye/hand and hardware checks.

# Apple HIG: Choose the representation people can use

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify what people need to understand or do with the content: compare data, read text, inspect imagery or interact with embedded web content. Enter that topic procedure.
2. Choose representation and hierarchy from the information task. Charts need an encoding/interaction decision; images need meaningful framing and alternatives; text needs reading/editing behavior; web views need integration boundaries.
3. Define the specific content states and accessible equivalents that the representation requires. Preserve context when detail, size or availability changes.
4. Deliver a revised content structure or implementable representation contract, and verify it against the supplied data and actual interface evidence.

# Apple HIG: End-to-end behavior and recovery

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Trace the person’s task from entry through completion, cancellation, interruption and recovery. Select the pattern procedure for the actual failure or desired behavior before selecting its controls.
2. Preserve the current work, selection and navigation context across the transitions that matter. Choose interruption or modality according to urgency and task scope, not visual emphasis.
3. For asynchronous or recurring work, separate current progress, eventual result, error recovery and unavailable capability. For audio/video/haptics, specify user control and environmental behavior.
4. Deliver a transition/state specification, a correction to the supplied flow, or ranked findings tied to observed steps. Test alternate exits and resumption, not just the success path.

name: apple-hig-edit-menus
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting selected-content editing commands and system edit-menu behavior.
---

# Make commands follow the selection

Read [the edit-menu guide](../../references/edit-menus.md). This procedure applies the source and distinguishes system behavior from product choices.

Inspect selected content types, editability, pasteboard state if available, platform/input, and create/review/adapt mode. Map Cut, Copy, Paste, Delete, custom actions, and undo to their actual scope. A screenshot cannot establish pasteboard or undo semantics.

Use the system edit menu and expected gestures. Remove/dim irrelevant commands; make Paste eligibility follow actual usable content. Distinguish Cut's transfer to the pasteboard from Delete's removal without copying. Group a few custom verbs with related standard actions, and preserve useful static-content copying while leaving ordinary control labels unselectable. Favor undo/redo over confirmation for ordinary edit actions.

Implement/specify command selection/paste/undo behavior, or review concrete semantic mismatches. Test both horizontal touch and vertical keyboard/pointer menus on iPad where relevant, preserving system pointer/menu shape while avoiding essential content obstruction. Mac uses standard Edit ordering. tvOS/watchOS lack this component; do not promise it as an entry solution there.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a transcript offers `Cut` on read-only text, `Paste` with no compatible content, and confirms every highlight removal. Decision: commands do not follow editability or clipboard state, while reversible work is interrupted. After: retain Copy and contextual lookup, expose editing only in an editable context, and make reversible highlight removal undoable.

Deliver the command/eligibility/undo contract and changed artifact. Verify empty selection, incompatible paste content, read-only content, Cut versus Delete pasteboard effects, and undo restoration. Fail for unintended loss, a command acting outside selection, or a falsely enabled action. State actual native pasteboard/gesture checks separately.

Use [undo-and-redo](../../../apple-hig-patterns/.topics/apple-hig-undo-and-redo/SKILL.md), [context-menus](../apple-hig-context-menus/SKILL.md), or [the-menu-bar](../apple-hig-the-menu-bar/SKILL.md) when those determine the command model.

name: apple-hig-focus-and-selection
description: Use when designing or reviewing keyboard, remote, or controller focus navigation, persistent selection, directional reachability, or disappearing focused items.
---

# Keep the interaction target distinct from the chosen value

Read [Focus and selection](../../references/focus-and-selection.md). Inspect platform/input, focus groups, selected state, dynamic content, and supplied implementation. Establish design/review/adaptation mode. The guide's component-focus model excludes iOS/watchOS; visionOS gaze hover is a different system.

Map focus movement separately from activation and persistent selection. Focus may select automatically only when that does not unexpectedly shift context; tvOS normally needs separate activation. Use system effects and avoid moving focus without input. If an item disappears during discrete directional movement, choose a nearby one-step target; for other input, hide the indicator rather than inventing the next destination.

On iPad, group custom content so Tab moves among logical groups and arrows move within them in expected reading order; prioritize the likely entry item. Ordinary content focus coexists with Full Keyboard Access for all controls. On TV, every interactive item needs directional reachability and room for enlarged focus art. Keep unfocused, focused, pressed, selected, and unavailable states distinct. Full-screen gestures should manipulate visible content rather than invisible focus.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a TV watchlist opens each item as focus passes over it and uses the same glow for focus and Saved. Decision: navigation must not activate content, and persistent choice must survive focus movement. After, focus raises/highlights the item, Select opens it, and a filled saved indicator remains as focus moves; unavailable items are inactive and unreachable.

Deliver a focus-route/group map and state contract or implementation. Walk each entry, direction, activation, return, and removal scenario. Fail if a control cannot be reached/exited, focus jumps without input, selected state vanishes with focus, or enlargement obscures information. Source inspection can establish intended grouping; actual focus engines, remote behavior, and Full Keyboard Access need supported execution.

Use [Remotes](../apple-hig-remotes/SKILL.md) for TV button meanings, [Keyboards](../apple-hig-keyboards/SKILL.md) for shortcuts/access, or [Eyes](../apple-hig-eyes/SKILL.md) when the request actually concerns gaze feedback.

---
name: apple-hig-text-views
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting multiline reading or editing surfaces, including selection, copying, text scaling, and input behavior.
---

# Define reading and editing independently

Read [the text-view guide](../../references/text-views.md). This operating procedure is application advice; use the guide for platform qualifications.

Inspect the supplied content, view/code, platform, and create/review/adapt request. Determine whether the text is long or formatted, editable or read-only, and useful to copy elsewhere. Identify scrolling ownership, text scaling, selection, and keyboard behavior from evidence. Do not assume a read-only view should also be unselectable.

Choose a text view for lengthy, specially formatted, or multiline editable content; use a label for short static text and a field for short entry. Preserve leading alignment and system color behavior where appropriate. Decide how long content reflows rather than truncating information the task requires. Support Dynamic Type and Bold Text without hardcoding a dense reading layout. Allow selection/copy for useful identifiers, addresses, errors, and prose people may reuse.

Implement the authorized view or produce an annotated reading/editing specification; in review identify the exact blocked task and replacement behavior. Match the iOS/iPadOS keyboard to expected input. On tvOS use text views for display and fields for editing, minimizing entry; do not copy a phone's long-form editor unchanged. Retain the user's framework and distinguish a desired capability from one verified in that framework.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a support app renders a long diagnostic report as clipped, unselectable labels. Decision: people need to read the full report and copy its reference numbers without editing them. After: a read-only multiline text view reflows and scrolls, permits selection/copy, and preserves contextual formatting; identifiers remain actual text.

Deliver the changed view plus its editability, copy, sizing, and scrolling contract. Verify a long paragraph, an unbroken identifier, enlarged text, and selection across lines; when editable, verify keyboard and saved content. Fail for inaccessible clipped content, accidental edits in read-only material, or useful text that cannot be copied. Mark VoiceOver/native keyboard execution unknown if only static inspection was possible.

Load [text-fields](../../../apple-hig-selection-and-input/.topics/apple-hig-text-fields/SKILL.md) for short entry, [labels](../../../apple-hig-layout-and-organization/.topics/apple-hig-labels/SKILL.md) for static captions, or [typography](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-typography/SKILL.md) when reading hierarchy needs deeper work.

---
name: apple-hig-undo-and-redo
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting reversible edits, history grouping, command labels, shortcuts, and visible restoration.
---

# Make the action being reversed predictable

Read [the undo/redo guide](../../references/undo-and-redo.md). This workflow is application advice; the source marks this pattern unsupported on tvOS/watchOS.

Inspect meaningful edit sequence, object identity, save/open boundaries, incremental controls, command access, platform, and create/review/adapt mode. # Edit menus Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/edit-menus) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Edit menus operate on selected text, images, files, and other content with commands such as copy, translation, and lookup. Data detection can add contextual actions, such as directions for an address. On iOS, selection gestures reveal a compact horizontal menu that can expand through a trailing chevron. iPad touch uses that layout; keyboard/pointer interactions open a vertical context-style menu. Mac offers contextual editing and the menu-bar Edit menu. visionOS offers pinch-and-hold horizontal or contextual editing. tvOS and watchOS do not provide this component. ## Best practices Use the system edit menu and its expected activation gestures. Remove or dim irrelevant commands, including selection-dependent actions without a selection and Paste when no paste content exists. Put custom commands near related standard commands, such as custom formatting after system formatting, and avoid excessive additions. Allow useful static content to copy, while normally keeping control labels unselectable. Support undo/redo rather than confirmations before menu actions. Avoid redundant editing controls that crowd out unfamiliar functionality. Distinguish Delete, which removes content, from Cut, which first places it on the pasteboard. ## Content Name custom actions with concise verbs or verb phrases. ## Platform considerations No additional visionOS rules are specified. Edit menus are unsupported in tvOS and watchOS. ### iOS, iPadOS Verify both horizontal touch and vertical keyboard/pointer presentations. The system chooses above/below-selection placement and its pointing indicator; adjust position when necessary to avoid essential content, without changing menu or pointer shape. ### macOS Follow the standard menu-bar Edit ordering documented in The menu bar. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Menus](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/menus) [Context menus](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/context-menus) [The menu bar](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/the-menu-bar) [Undo and redo](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/undo-and-redo) #### Developer documentation — UIKit — AppKit ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: June 21, 2023, September 14, 2022.

# Focus and selection Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Focus visually identifies an interaction target for component-based navigation with keyboards, remotes, and controllers. Focus can select an item automatically, except where selection would shift context; tvOS normally requires separate activation. Rings/highlights on tablet/Mac and depth/parallax on TV reflect their platform focus models. ## Best practices Use system focus effects unless customization is essential. Do not move focus without input. If a focused item disappears during discrete directional navigation, move to a nearby one-step item; with other input, hide the indicator rather than guessing the next target. Follow platform reachability conventions: keyboard content focus on iPad/Mac coexists with Full Keyboard Access for all controls, whereas tvOS requires directional access to every interactive item. Use rings for text/search and usually full-row highlights for lists/collections. Standard focused/unfocused selection colors preserve active context. ## Platform considerations The source marks focus unsupported on iOS/watchOS in this topic’s sense. ### iPadOS Since iPadOS 15, Tab moves between focus groups and arrows move inside a group. Group custom views to produce expected reading order, normally leading-to-trailing then top-to-bottom; a vertical stack may need one focus-group container. Set priority so a likely primary item receives focus when a group is entered. Halo effects outline an item and can be refined for shape, clipping, or badge overlap. A content-configured cell’s highlighted accent appearance is separate from a focus effect. ### tvOS In full-screen content, gestures should act on the content rather than invisible focus. Use component focus for menus instead of a tiny free pointer; a gameplay-specific pointer must be conspicuous and integrated. Allow room and high-resolution art for enlarged focus states. Represent unfocused (receded), focused (raised/lit/moving), pressed (immediate feedback), selected (persistent choice such as filled favorite), and unavailable (inactive and unreachable) states distinctly. ### visionOS Connected keyboards/controllers use the same focus system family. Looking at content uses hover feedback instead; do not treat gaze hover as keyboard/controller focus. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: October 24, 2023, June 21, 2023.

# Text views Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/text-views) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. A text view handles multiple lines, rich styling, scrolling, and optional editing. Content normally starts at the leading edge and uses the system label color. Editing invokes a keyboard in iOS, iPadOS, and visionOS. ## Best practices Choose a text view for lengthy, editable, or specially formatted content. Use a label for short static text and a text field for short editable input. Styling must preserve reading comfort: adopt Dynamic Type and check accessibility settings such as Bold Text. Allow selection and copying when the text contains information people may need elsewhere, including error details, identifiers, or network addresses. ## Platform considerations The source adds no separate macOS, visionOS, or watchOS rules. ### iOS, iPadOS Match the virtual keyboard to the expected input so entry is efficient and relevant characters are easy to reach. ### tvOS Use text views to display content. Editable tvOS text belongs in text fields; the platform deliberately minimizes text entry. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Labels](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/labels) [Text fields](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/text-fields) [Combo boxes](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/combo-boxes) #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — UIKit — AppKit ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: June 5, 2023.

# Undo and redo Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/undo-and-redo) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Undo/redo supports safe exploration when people can predict the affected action and see its outcome. ## Best practices Describe the target in menu labels or the iPhone shake confirmation. Reveal offscreen changes, for example scrolling to restored text, so people do not repeat undo because nothing seemed to happen. Avoid arbitrary history limits; support the meaningful action sequence since opening or saving. Group related incremental adjustments when a batch undo helps, and consider reverting a larger set. Use standard menus/shortcuts/gestures first; add dedicated buttons only when needed, with standard symbols in a toolbar. ## Platform considerations No additional visionOS rules are specified. Undo/redo is unsupported in tvOS and watchOS in this pattern guidance. ### iOS, iPadOS Preserve standard three-finger swipe and iPhone shake behavior. The system supplies Undo/Redo plus a trailing space in alert titles; add only one or two precise words describing the operation. ### macOS Put commands at the top of Edit and preserve Command-Z for Undo and Shift-Command-Z for Redo. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Feedback](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/feedback) [Pointing devices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/pointing-devices) [Standard keyboard shortcuts](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/keyboards#Standard-keyboard-shortcuts) [Edit menu](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/the-menu-bar#Edit-menu) #### Developer documentation — Foundation #### Videos

item.text: The brief identifies selection loss, invalid Paste availability, unsafe Cut behavior, and unrelated account and bulk-delete commands. I’ll replace the bespoke menu with a system edit-menu contract and define command eligibility, failure handling, and undo recovery.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "cat > interface.md <<'EOF'
# iPad annotation text-editing specification

Platform: iPadOS. Retain the custom annotation view; integrate the system edit menu for annotation text. This is a revised behavior specification, not an SDK implementation. No framework or deployment target is supplied.

## Scope and presentation

Use standard selection and edit-menu activation gestures. Touch presents the system horizontal edit menu; keyboard/pointer activation uses the system vertical presentation. Preserve system menu shape and pointing indicator. Anchor to the selected range or insertion point; adjust placement only as needed to avoid essential content. Do not duplicate standard editing actions in a bespoke menu.

Remove Rename Account and hidden Delete All from this text-editing menu. Account naming and bulk deletion have different scopes and are outside this repair; neither may be invoked by a text command. Do not silently reinterpret Delete All as selection deletion. Add no custom commands in this revision.

## Selection and command target

Maintain annotation identity, text revision, selected range or insertion point, and editability independently of menu focus. Opening, navigating, dismissing, or cancelling the menu must not clear or move the selection. Keep the selected range visibly identified while the menu has focus, and return editing focus to that range on dismissal. Opening a menu over an existing selection operates on that selection; an intentional selection gesture may establish a new range before opening it.

A command targets only the active annotation and its validated range, never the whole document or account. Revalidate target identity, revision, editability, and command eligibility at invocation and before committing any asynchronous result. If the annotation disappears, its revision changes, or the selection changes while work is pending, cancel the pending mutation rather than apply it to a guessed range. Keep any still-valid current selection. Do not move focus to another annotation automatically.

## Command contract

Unavailable actions are omitted from the edit menu. Every alternate invocation must use the same eligibility rules and refuse stale or unavailable actions without mutation.

| Command | Eligibility | Successful result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Copy | Nonempty selected text, including useful read-only text | Write selected text to the pasteboard; leave text and selection unchanged. |
| Cut | Nonempty selected text in an editable annotation | Successfully copy the selected text first, then remove precisely that range as one undoable edit; collapse the insertion point at the removed range's start. |
| Paste | Editable annotation with a valid insertion point/range and compatible usable paste content | Insert at the caret or replace only the selection; leave the caret immediately after the inserted text. One undoable edit. |
| Delete | Nonempty selected text in an editable annotation | Remove only the selection without writing to the pasteboard; collapse the caret at its start. One undoable edit. |
| Select All | Active annotation contains text and is not already fully selected | Select all text in this annotation only; do not modify text or history. |

Product format decision: this repair accepts nonempty plain text, including a usable plain-text representation supplied with rich text. It does not paste images, files, or rich formatting. Empty data, unsupported-only representations, and unreadable content do not qualify. Use platform-supported eligibility mechanisms; do not read clipboard payloads merely to open the menu. If compatibility cannot yet be established, omit Paste until it can. Recheck and decode content on invocation; a pasteboard change or read failure must leave text and selection intact. Select a supported text representation deterministically and insert it once.

With an empty selection, omit Copy, Cut, and Delete. Paste may remain available at a valid caret. In read-only text, allow selection, Copy, and Select All, but omit Cut, Paste, and Delete. Ordinary control labels remain unselectable. A failed Copy leaves the document unchanged. A failed Cut transfer never removes text. If copying succeeds but target validation or removal fails, retain document text; the pasteboard may contain the copied text. Never claim the document was cut in that case. Failed operations add no undo entry. Preserve the selection and provide a concise failure message, such as “Couldn’t cut text. Your text is unchanged.”

## Recovery and history

Prefer undo/redo to confirmation for these ordinary edits. Cut, Paste (including replacement), and Delete each record one atomic inverse containing the annotation identity, previous text, and selection. Undo restores the exact prior text and selection; Redo restores the successful edit and resulting caret. Neither Undo nor Redo rewrites the pasteboard. Copy, selection movement, and menu presentation create no history entries.

Preserve standard iPadOS undo/redo interactions, including three-finger gestures, without intercepting them for annotation gestures. Describe the operation with precise names such as Cut Text, Paste Text, and Delete Text; let the system supply its own Undo/Redo prefix where applicable. Reveal restored offscreen text with minimal scrolling. A new successful edit after Undo clears the redo branch. Retain meaningful history for the open document across saves; closing ends this session's history. Do not impose an arbitrary shallow limit that loses the meaningful edit sequence.

## Verification contract

The acceptance scenarios and their execution status are recorded in result.md. Native rendering, input, pasteboard integration, and recovery must be verified in an implemented iPad app before claiming runtime compliance.

## Guidance basis

System menu, command relevance, Cut/Delete distinction, and iPad presentation follow [Edit menus](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/edit-menus#Best-practices). Selection remains independent of transient focus, consistent with [Focus and selection](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection#Best-practices). Useful read-only text remains copyable per [Text views](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/text-views#Best-practices). Recovery, meaningful history, operation naming, and revealing restored content follow [Undo and redo](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/undo-and-redo#Best-practices). Clipboard formats, failure atomicity, stale-target cancellation, exact selection restoration, and session history boundaries are concrete product decisions supporting those principles, not quoted HIG API guarantees.
EOF"

# Repair outcome

Patched interface.md in place, replacing the original single-paragraph brief with an implementable command, selection, failure, and recovery specification for the custom iPad annotation view.

## Decisions and changes

- Replace the bespoke long-press menu with the system edit menu, preserving horizontal touch and vertical keyboard/pointer presentations and system placement/shape behavior.
- Remove Rename Account and hidden Delete All from the selection menu. Their broader tasks remain outside this repair. Delete now explicitly means selected text only.
- Preserve selection independently of menu focus and validate annotation identity, revision, and range before committing changes.
- Specify Copy, Cut, Paste, Delete, and Select All eligibility for selected, empty, and read-only states. Paste accepts usable nonempty plain text; unsupported data cannot enable it.
- Make Cut copy successfully before removal, preserve text on failures, and distinguish Delete's lack of pasteboard writes. Make successful mutations atomic undo units with exact text/selection restoration and visible recovery.

The format policy, transaction rules, stale-target handling, and history lifetime are product decisions. HIG supports the interaction principles; it does not establish an SDK implementation or prescribe these exact transaction mechanics.

## Worked before/after

Start with editable annotation "'`Review blue notes`, selecting `blue`, and a pasteboard containing only an image.

Before (from the supplied brief): opening the bespoke menu loses selection, offers Rename Account and hidden Delete All, and shows Paste despite unsupported data. Cut removes selection before copying succeeds and is irreversible. This is the specified failure model, not a reproduced device trace.

After (required behavior): opening the system menu preserves `blue` as the command target. Copy, Cut, Delete, and Select All are eligible; Paste is omitted because an image alone is unsupported. No account or bulk-delete command appears. If Cut'"'s pasteboard write fails, text remains "'`Review blue notes`, `blue` remains selected, and history is unchanged. If it succeeds, the pasteboard contains `blue`, the annotation becomes `Review  notes`, and the caret sits where `blue` began. Undo restores `Review blue notes` with `blue` selected; Redo removes it again. Neither history action changes the pasteboard. With compatible text `green`, Paste replacing `blue` instead yields `Review green notes`; one Undo restores `blue` and its selection.

## Acceptance checks

Static specification checks — passed by inspection of the revised artifact:

- All supplied defects have explicit replacement rules: unrelated commands, selection loss, unsupported Paste, and destructive Cut ordering.
- Command table covers empty selection, read-only content, exact target scope, and Cut versus Delete pasteboard effects.
- Failed operations preserve content and create no history entry; stale asynchronous targets cannot mutate a new range.
- Undo/Redo units, restored selection, reveal behavior, redo invalidation, and save/close boundaries are defined.

Runtime acceptance — not executed; expected results for implementation validation:

| Scenario | Required result |
| --- | --- |
| Open, navigate, dismiss, and reopen menu on multiline selection | Same range and annotation remain selected; no edit or history entry. |
| Empty selection and empty annotation | Copy/Cut/Delete absent; Select All absent for empty text; compatible Paste available only at a valid editable caret. |
| Read-only prose or identifier | Selection and Copy work, including across lines; no mutation commands. |
| Empty, image-only, unreadable, mixed rich/plain, and valid text pasteboard | Only usable nonempty plain text qualifies; replacement/insertion occurs exactly once. |
| Clipboard changes after menu opens | Eligibility is revalidated; failed decoding leaves text and selection intact. |
| Inject Copy/Cut transfer failure or removal failure | No text loss or history entry; after successful copy followed by failed removal, copied clipboard text may remain. |
| Delete selected text with known clipboard sentinel | Only selected text disappears; clipboard sentinel remains unchanged. |
| Change selection/revision or remove annotation during pending transfer | No stale mutation or guessed new target. |

| Undo, then new edit; save; close/reopen | Redo branch cleared by new edit; save retains history; reopened session starts fresh. |
| Undo an offscreen deletion | Restored text becomes visible without unnecessary context loss. |
| Touch and keyboard/pointer menu activation | Native horizontal/vertical presentations, system pointer shape, essential content unobscured, and focus returns to the text range. |

Native pasteboard permissions, menu geometry, focus return, gesture integration, assistive-technology behavior, and SDK availability remain unverified. This work repairs the specification; it does not demonstrate implementation compliance.

interface.md:1:# iPad annotation text-editing specification
interface.md:5:## Scope and presentation
interface.md:11:## Selection and command target
interface.md:17:## Command contract
interface.md:24:| Cut | Nonempty selected text in an editable annotation | Successfully copy the selected text first, then remove precisely that range as one undoable edit; collapse the insertion point at the removed range's start. |
interface.md:25:| Paste | Editable annotation with a valid insertion point/range and compatible usable paste content | Insert at the caret or replace only the selection; leave the caret immediately after the inserted text. One undoable edit. |
interface.md:29:Product format decision: this repair accepts nonempty plain text, including a usable plain-text representation supplied with rich text. It does not paste images, files, or rich formatting. Empty data, unsupported-only representations, and unreadable content do not qualify. Use platform-supported eligibility mechanisms; do not read clipboard payloads merely to open the menu. If compatibility cannot yet be established, omit Paste until it can. Recheck and decode content on invocation; a pasteboard change or read failure must leave text and selection intact. Select a supported text representation deterministically and insert it once.
interface.md:31:With an empty selection, omit Copy, Cut, and Delete. Paste may remain available at a valid caret. In read-only text, allow selection, Copy, and Select All, but omit Cut, Paste, and Delete. Ordinary control labels remain unselectable. A failed Copy leaves the document unchanged. A failed Cut transfer never removes text. If copying succeeds but target validation or removal fails, retain document text; the pasteboard may contain the copied text. Never claim the document was cut in that case. Failed operations add no undo entry. Preserve the selection and provide a concise failure message, such as “Couldn’t cut text. Your text is unchanged.”
interface.md:33:## Recovery and history
interface.md:35:Prefer undo/redo to confirmation for these ordinary edits. Cut, Paste (including replacement), and Delete each record one atomic inverse containing the annotation identity, previous text, and selection. Undo restores the exact prior text and selection; Redo restores the successful edit and resulting caret. Neither Undo nor Redo rewrites the pasteboard. Copy, selection movement, and menu presentation create no history entries.
interface.md:37:Preserve standard iPadOS undo/redo interactions, including three-finger gestures, without intercepting them for annotation gestures. Describe the operation with precise names such as Cut Text, Paste Text, and Delete Text; let the system supply its own Undo/Redo prefix where applicable. Reveal restored offscreen text with minimal scrolling. A new successful edit after Undo clears the redo branch. Retain meaningful history for the open document across saves; closing ends this session's history. Do not impose an arbitrary shallow limit that loses the meaningful edit sequence.
interface.md:39:## Verification contract
interface.md:43:## Guidance basis
interface.md:45:System menu, command relevance, Cut/Delete distinction, and iPad presentation follow [Edit menus](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/edit-menus#Best-practices). Selection remains independent of transient focus, consistent with [Focus and selection](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection#Best-practices). Useful read-only text remains copyable per [Text views](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/text-views#Best-practices). Recovery, meaningful history, operation naming, and revealing restored content follow [Undo and redo](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/undo-and-redo#Best-practices). Clipboard formats, failure atomicity, stale-target cancellation, exact selection restoration, and session history boundaries are concrete product decisions supporting those principles, not quoted HIG API guarantees.
